Notes

Ready-made advice keeps arriving, but the speaker’s body, jokes and creative work refuse to fit its reassuring shapes.

静下心听

The opening answers “what should I do?” with a small instruction to quiet the mind and listen. But the verse soon says not to speak, not to act and not to leave. The first directive can sound soothing until later commands reveal how easily guidance becomes restraint. The song keeps testing whether familiar advice makes room for him or closes it.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
头发掉到嘴里

An awkward, unglamorous bodily detail interrupts the instruction to become calm. Hair in the mouth and a body growing light do not add up to a named condition; they convey discomfort through sensations that are hard to organize. That matters beside the question of how to sort things out: the body presents the same problem as the crowded mind.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
未解之谜

未解之谜 is the sort of formal heading given to a puzzle that has not been explained. The verse applies it to unease picked up somewhere unfamiliar. It momentarily makes private discomfort sound like a documentary topic. A few lines later the documentary becomes explicit, linking the search for explanations to the making of a story about a life.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
走一步算一步

走一步算一步 means deciding what to do at each step as events unfold, without a settled plan for what follows. English “one step at a time” can sound calmly methodical; the Chinese has more of “we’ll work it out as we go.” Next to unexplained sickness and mysteries, the line names an improvised survival method rather than confidence that the route is known.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
就没有读过书

读书 can mean reading books or studying, so the line is broader than an inventory of leisure reading. The microphone marks a change in where knowledge comes from. The next sequence of inherited sayings complicates the joke: he can disclaim book-learning while demonstrating how much familiar cultural language is already lodged in ordinary speech.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
忆苦思甜

忆苦思甜 means recalling hardship in order to appreciate a sweeter present. It also belongs to the vocabulary of Chinese moral and political education: institutions use the phrase for activities teaching gratitude through remembering difficult times. Here it joins a string of familiar maxims, yet the song supplies no convincingly sweet present. The next claim is that he already knows the routine.

  • Ezhou Education Bureau: an 忆苦思甜 activity
活到老学到老

活到老学到老 literally keeps living and learning going until old age. It follows the claim that picking up a microphone ended his book-reading. The maxim can therefore sound both corrective and dryly comic: he may not be studying books, but experience is certainly continuing to teach him. The stock expression offers wisdom while the surrounding lines distrust stock routines.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
轻车熟路

轻车熟路 pictures a light, easily handled vehicle on a familiar road. As an idiom it means being practiced and comfortable with a task. Put after “take it one step at a time,” it is a striking change in claimed competence. Before that confidence can settle, “you cannot run” turns the route into somewhere he may be forced to remain.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
你娃会遭

娃 is a child, but 你娃 can address a person directly in familiar or scolding regional speech. 遭, left without a full outcome, means they will come to harm or get what is coming to them. The warning is less polished than the adjacent four-character sayings. It sounds like somebody speaking close enough to threaten you in ordinary language.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
报应会到

报应 is the return of consequences for one’s actions, often understood as moral recompense. Here it follows prohibitions on speech and action, making restraint sound enforced by a punishment that need not be immediately visible. The sentence supplies certainty about the future precisely where the speaker’s own attempts to plan have been uncertain.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
一部纪录片

The sudden film vocabulary pulls the preceding material into the frame of a work being made. The director’s early start is comically mundane after threats of retribution. It also places labor behind the image: somebody has to get up and organize this apparently unruly experience. The next untold jokes show that the material still exceeds the finished telling.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
想到了很多笑话

He has jokes ready but has not had time to tell them. Soon a sensitive child laughs to look strong. Laughter therefore appears twice as something whose outward presence can mislead: jokes remain unheard, while a heard laugh conceals pain. The song makes a distinction between having comic material and being able to use it freely.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
大大咧咧

大大咧咧 describes an apparently casual, rough-and-ready, unconcerned manner. It is paired here with a 敏感的娃, a sensitive kid, and then explicitly explained as acting strong. The outward laugh is not a contradiction to be solved: the lyric tells us it is the method of concealment. This is one of the tape’s clearest small portraits of performance as self-protection.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
拳脚都被束缚

拳脚 means fists and feet and can evoke the ability to act or show one’s skills. Their restraint leads directly to the contrast between beautiful ideals and cruel reality. The phrase brings the complaint back into the body: artistic frustration is not only difficulty finding an idea, but being unable to put one’s capacities into motion.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
创作思想

创作思想 is formal language for the ideas informing a creative work. The profanity punctures that high register, then the ashtray reduces the whole discussion to an object that holds spent residue. The ending is more pointed than “art is hard”: even the language used to dignify creation seems unable to save what it describes from becoming waste.

About Jackzebra and this mixtape

Zhuang Zhuang Mixtape arrived on Surf Gang on October 2, 2026: 55 tracks, opening with Sour and closing with Sweet. Its cast widens from YoungQueenz on Poker Face to User116, Effie, kuru, yoyi, 春 and 南部犯罪份子. Aghast has a production credit on every track from Hitman through Snatch, giving that stretch a shared collaborator behind its changing scenes.

Surf Gang release · Artist credits

Jackzebra told AVYSS that he writes while singing over a beat he has listened to repeatedly, keeping the images in his head central. He values the room Mandarin leaves for indirect meanings. Listen for ordinary phrases becoming physical scenes: familiarity becomes cooking, authority becomes family seniority, and a tired saying suddenly turns into a threat.

AVYSS interview, 2024

In STATIC, he describes mixtapes as a format for letting ideas flow, reserving an official debut album for later. In a separate conversation about Above & Beyond, he compared that earlier tape to a collection of his producer friends’ work. The credits here likewise reward attention: long-running collaborators sit alongside guests working in Mandarin, Korean and English.

STATIC interview · Sabukaru interview, 2025

The small details connect to his stated interests: he has described playing Temple Run in transit and before shows, watching Top Boy, and wanting to score White Oleander. These give the songs specific points of contact with his life. The notes follow those connections alongside the lyrics’ jokes, invented scenes and competing voices.

His recommendations in Perfectly Imperfect · Dazed interview, 2025 · Interview questionnaire, 2025

Jackzebra has pushed back on being made to represent all of China’s underground. These notes stay close to the words: what an expression usually means, what changes in this line, and how another song answers it. Cultural references have sources; interpretations rest on details you can hear or read in the song.
